newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle trade thin at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle trade thin at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets Monday were steady in thin trading, with most feedlot sources not expecting large-scale packer buying until later this week.
Scattered buying was reported at $72.00 per cwt, steady with last week's top price, sources said.
About 600 head were sold in Kansas and 100 to 200 in the Panhandle area, USDA and private sources said.

Once the bulk of this week's cattle start trading, they were expected to bring $73.00 because of tight supplies of finished cattle on showlists this week and continued strong beef demand, sources said.
Not only were showlists smaller this week than last week, but many were said to have a large number of 'green' or unfinished cattle, sources said.
Showlists in the Panhandle area were pegged near 67,000 head, down 8,000 from last week. The Kansas showlist was estimated near 52,000 head, down 2,800 from last week.
Gains could be tempered by light packer demand, with many plants reportedly well supplied with live inventory following last week's brisk volume, sources said.
